facts.statement: Roxochampsa lived during the Late Cretaceous period.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous~

facts.statement: Roxochampsa was an extinct itasuchid notosuchian crocodyliform found in Late Cretaceous Brazil.
facts.quote: Roxochampsa is an extinct genus of itasuchid notosuchian from the Late Cretaceous of Brazil.

facts.statement: Fossils of Roxochampsa have been discovered in the Adamantina and Presidente Prudente Formations.
facts.quote: Fossil remains have been found in the sediments of the Adamantina and Presidente Prudente Formations

facts.statement: The species was originally described as Goniopholis paulistanus.
facts.quote: were originally described as a species of Goniopholis.

facts.statement: Roxochampsa possessed narrow, elongated jaws indicating a mesorostrine and flattened skull shape.
facts.quote: Roxochampsa had narrow and elongated jaws that indicate a mesorostrine and flattened skull shape.

facts.statement: Roxochampsa had interlocking teeth with carinae and crenulations, making it a pseudo-ziphodont.
facts.quote: The teeth were interlocking as in modern crocodiles and bear carinae with crenulations, making it pseudo-ziphodont.

facts.statement: Roxochampsa's teeth featured prominent crenulated ridges forming secondary cutting edges alongside main carinae.
facts.quote: Among the most distinguishing features of Roxochampsa is the fact that the teeth furthermore bear prominent crenulated ridges that form secondary cutting edges in addition to the main carinae.

facts.statement: Teeth similar to Roxochampsa were recognized from Brazil's Bauru Group as early as 1911.
facts.quote: Teeth similar to those of Roxochampsa have been recognized from Brazil's Bauru Group as early as 1911

facts.statement: Two teeth (DGM 259-R and DGM 258-R) were recovered in 1935 near Amandaba city in Mirandópolis.
facts.quote: two teeth (DGM 259-R and DGM 258-R) recovered in 1935 near Amandaba city in Mirandópolis

facts.statement: The species was described as Goniopholis paulistanus in 1936 by Mathias Gonçalves de Oliveria Roxo.
facts.quote: This material was described under the name Goniopholis paulistanus in 1936 by Mathias Gonçalves de Oliveria Roxo

facts.statement: New jaw material was described from the Presidente Prudente Formation in Alfredo Marcondes municipality in 2018.
facts.quote: Pinheiro et al. (2018) described new jaw material from the Presidente Prudente Formation of the Alfredo Marcondes municipality in São Paulo state

facts.statement: The name Roxochampsa combines the Greek word for crocodile with the last name of the original describer, Mathias Gonçalves de Oliveria Roxo.
facts.quote: The name Roxochampsa combines the Greek suffix Xαμψαι (champsa), which translates to "crocodile" and the last name of Mathias Gonçalves de Oliveria Roxo, who originally described the species as Goniopholis paulistanus in 1936.

facts.statement: Roxochampsa is interpreted as having a platyrostral and mesorostrine skull of moderate length and flattened morphology.
facts.quote: In the 2018 description of Roxochampsa, Pinheiro and colleagues interpret it as having been platyrostral and mesorostrine, which translates to a skull of moderate or "normal" length with an overall flattened morphology likened to other itasuchids and modern crocodiles.

facts.statement: The lower jaw of Roxochampsa shows two distinct waves in lateral view, one peaking at the fourth and fifth teeth and another between the eighth and fourteenth.
facts.quote: In lateral view the lower jaw shows two distinct waves that festoon the mandible, one that peaks around the level of the fourth and fifth dentary teeth and a second, shallower peak between the eight and fourteenth teeth.

facts.statement: The Roxochampsa mandible expands outward at a 25° angle, giving it the shape of a narrow Y.
facts.quote: the mandible expands outward at a 25° angle with a convex outline, giving the entire mandible the shape of a narrow Y.

facts.statement: The symphysis of Roxochampsa is moderately long and thought to extend across nine teeth.
facts.quote: The symphysis is moderately long as in Itasuchus and Pepesuchus and is thought to extend across nine teeth

facts.statement: Some teeth similar to Roxochampsa were once referred to the family Trematochampsidae after its establishment in 1974.
facts.quote: After Eric Buffetaut established the family Trematochampsidae in 1974, several teeth of similar morphology to those of Goniopholis paulistanus were instead referred to this family

facts.statement: Researchers warn that tooth crowns alone are insufficient for recognizing specific clades or species without substantial fossil remains.
facts.quote: In this study, the team warned that though useful in recognizing broader morphotypes, tooth crowns alone are not sufficient in recognizing specific clades or even species and would require either the support of a phylogenetic framework of more substantial fossil remains.

facts.statement: Roxochampsa is estimated to have possessed 19 teeth in each half of its lower jaw.
facts.quote: Based on the referred mandibular remains Roxochampsa is thought to have had 19 teeth in each hemimandible

facts.statement: The front teeth of Roxochampsa were procumbent, pointing forward and oriented sub-horizontally relative to the jaw joint.
facts.quote: The first teeth in the jaw are procumbent, meaning they were pointing more forward and oriented sub-horizontal relative to the mandibular symphysis

facts.statement: Roxochampsa teeth exhibit "false ziphodonty," characterized by crenulated cutting edges rather than the distinct denticles found in true ziphodonty.
facts.quote: The teeth furthermore display "false ziphodonty", which means that the cutting edges of the teeth (carinae) bear crenulations, as opposed to the distinct denticles that define true ziphodonty

facts.statement: The 12th lower jaw tooth of Roxochampsa features blunt, overlapping, and hooked structures extending from the middle to the top quarter of the crown, transitioning to a rugose, "scaly" texture at the apex.
facts.quote: The crown of the 12th dentary tooth furthermore features blunt, overlapping and hooked structures that extend from the middle of the crown through its topmost quarter before transitioning into what Pinheiro and colleagues describe as a rugose and "scaly" texture at the tooth's apex

facts.statement: Evidence from jaw scars suggests Roxochampsa possessed interlocking dentition similar to modern crocodiles, known as "crocodyloid occlusion."
facts.quote: Based on these, all three taxa would have had interlocking dentition similar to modern crocodiles, which is why this particular pattern is also referred to as "crocodyloid occlusion"

facts.statement: Researchers estimate a minimum lower jaw length of 25 cm for Roxochampsa, though the lack of preserved posterior parts suggests the actual length may have been greater.
facts.quote: Pinheiro and colleagues estimate a minimum mandibular length of 25 cm, but concede that since none of the posterior parts are actually preserved in the more complete specimens it may have been even longer

facts.statement: Comparisons with the related genus Caririsuchus suggest Roxochampsa reached an approximate total body size of 1 to 2 meters.
facts.quote: Comparing the mandibular length estimate with the proportions of the much more complete Caririsuchus yields an approximate size of 1-2 m

facts.statement: A semi-strict consensus analysis by Wilberg and colleagues suggests that Roxochampsa and Amargasuchus may be sister taxa, though this remains a hypothesis to resolve phylogenetic uncertainty.
facts.quote: Wilberg and colleagues furthermore provide a semi-strict consensus alternative in an attempt to resolve this polytomy, which indicates that Roxochampsa and Amargasuchus may be sister taxa

facts.statement: Recent studies by Ruiz et al. (2024) and Wilberg et al. (2025) have recovered nearly identical evolutionary groupings containing Roxochampsa, though they applied different family names.
facts.quote: Since then the contents of both families have similarly expanded, resulting in Ruiz et al. (2024) and Wilberg et al. (2025) recovering almost identical clades but under different names

facts.statement: Roxochampsa was likely a semi-aquatic predator with a generalist diet including fish, turtles, hard-shelled animals, and small to mid-sized terrestrial vertebrates.
facts.quote: Roxochampsa is thought to have been a semi-aquatic predator with a relatively generalist diet consisting of fish, turtles and other hard-shelled animals, small to mid-sized terrestrial vertebrates and possibly the occasional carcass.

facts.statement: A 2021 study suggests Roxochampsa scavenged sauropod dinosaurs based on bite marks found on a fossil from the Presidente Prudente Formation.
facts.quote: The idea of Roxochampsa engaging in scavenging is furthermore supported by a 2021 paper published by Pereira and colleagues in which the team describes the fragmentary epiphysis of a sauropod dinosaur from the Presidente Prudente Formation bearing various bite marks.

facts.statement: Bite marks on a sauropod fossil show shallow grooves matching modern crocodilian feeding traces rather than those of theropods or mammals, supporting the scavenging hypothesis.
facts.quote: The oval shape and lack of marks left by true serrations excludes both larger theropods and scavenging mammals. Instead the additional shallow grooves present on the fossil match the kinds of traces left by modern crocodylians when grasping bone and thrashing their head around in order to rip a carcass into smaller pieces.

facts.statement: Evidence for the 'death rolling' behavior seen in modern crocodiles is absent in Roxochampsa and remains unconfirmed in its relatives.
facts.quote: Death rolling, the spinning maneuver performed by modern crocodiles, is not supported due to the absence of other characteristic traces and is unconfirmed behavior in itasuchids.

facts.statement: Roxochampsa's teeth were adapted to stab and crush prey rather than impale it, unlike specialized fish-eaters like gharials.
facts.quote: Given the mesorostrine proportions and inferred generalist diet, the interlocking teeth of Roxochampsa would have served to stab and crush prey rather than to strike and impale as in gharials.

facts.statement: The relatively blunt shape of Roxochampsa's posterior teeth argues against a specialized diet of fish.
facts.quote: Another pointer against a specialized piscivorous diet comes in the shape of the posterior teeth, which despite the narrowness of the jaws were relatively blunt.

facts.statement: Roxochampsa likely had the jaw strength to crack shells of molluscs, crabs, turtles, and possibly bone.
facts.quote: This, combined with the greater force generated in this part jaw, would allow it to crack the shells of hard-shelled prey, which may include various molluscs, crabs, small turtles and perhaps even bone.

facts.statement: Crenulated ridges on Roxochampsa's teeth may have aided in slicing prey, improving grip on wet animals, or strengthening the enamel.
facts.quote: The distinct ornamentation of the teeth with crenulated ridges may have played a role in the diet and prey capture methods of Roxochampsa as well.

facts.statement: Roxochampsa fossils are found in the Presidente Prudente and Upper Adamantina formations of Brazil's Bauru Group.
facts.quote: Roxochampsa is known from two geological formations of Brazil′s Bauru Group, the Late Campanian to Early Maastrichtian Presidente Prudente Formation and the Early Maastrichtian Upper Adamantina Formation.

facts.statement: The environment where Roxochampsa lived featured meandering rivers, sandy bars, and floodplains under an arid to semi-arid climate.
facts.quote: The former is interpreted to have featured high sinuosity meandering river channels during the time of its deposition with sandy bars, crevasse splay and floodplains with an arid to semi-arid climate.

facts.statement: Later layers of the Adamantina Formation indicate an environment with both braided and meandering rivers.
facts.quote: The Adamantina Formation preserves what was once an environment defined by braided and meandering rivers in its later strata.

facts.statement: The primary Roxochampsa site (AM1) also preserves fossils of abelisaurid and coelurosaur theropods.
facts.quote: The site that yielded the best remains of Roxochamspa, AM1 of the Presidente Prudente Formation, preserves the fossils of several dinosaurs. Theropods are represented by a abelisaurid and an indeterminate coelurosaur.

facts.statement: The Presidente Prudente Formation contains fossils of the sauropod Austroposeidon and other Aeolosaurini.
facts.quote: The Presidente Prudente Formation also yielded the sauropod Austroposeidon alongside other remains of the clade Aeolosaurini.

facts.statement: Roxochampsa belongs to the family Itasuchidae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Itasuchidae

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Roxochampsa is Roxochampsa paulistanus.
facts.quote: Type species: Roxochampsa paulistanus

facts.statement: Roxochampsa lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The genus Roxochampsa was named by Piacentini Pinheiro and colleagues in 2018.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Roxochampsa (genus), Piacentini Pinheiro et al. 2018

facts.statement: There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Roxochampsa in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 3
